By applying agglomerative clustering to a downsampled universe of 40,000 devices, the study isolates distinct behavioral subpopulations. These clusters are then compared against national and seed baselines to compute behavioral index profiles. The key duality lies in translating abstract digital engagement into concrete physical attendance probabilities. The failure mode arises when geolocation data misrepresents true attendance, leading to spurious correlations. The methodological rigor ensures reproducibility by pre-specifying analysis steps before data collection, mitigating confirmation bias. The derived kernel operates under the assumption that digital behavior is a proxy for real-world purchasing intent, validated through geofenced attendance data.
